title: Bounded field-writing machine
statement: For any types $Q$ and $T$ with decidable equality, there are a natural number $K$, a finite state set $S$ with decidable equality, a machine $R$ with $K+1$ work tapes over symbols that encode either Boolean digits, marked Boolean work cells, states from $Q$, or tags from $T$, designated states $entry,exit\in S$, and a natural number $C$, with the following property. For every $k$, every embedding $\iota:\{0,\ldots,K\}\hookrightarrow\{0,\ldots,k-1\}$, every tape index $dst$ outside the image of $\iota$, every Boolean word $x$, and every configuration $d$ on input $x$ encoded as digit symbols, if $d$ is in state $entry$, its input head is at position $1$, and all cells of the work tapes indexed by $\iota$ are blank, then the embedded machine reaches a configuration equal to $d$ except that its state is $exit$ and tape $dst$ stores the binary expansion of $|x|+1$ starting at its initial head position (all other tape cells retain their contents). It does so at some time $t\le C(|x|+1)$, does not visit state $exit$ earlier, and throughout the first $t$ steps every work-tape head stays within distance $C(\operatorname{bits}(|x|+1)+1)$ of its initial position.
hypotheses_covered: Finite state set $S$ with decidable equality exists
Embedding of $K+1$ tape indices into $k$ tape indices
Destination tape index lies outside the embedding image
Input is a Boolean word encoded as digit symbols
Every cell on each embedded tape is blank
Final configuration and written binary word
